# bigalgebra

# Arithmetic routines for native R matrices and big.matrix objects

## Frédéric Bertrand, Michael J. Kane, Bryan Lewis, John W. Emerson

<https://doi.org/10.32614/CRAN.package.bigalgebra>

`bigalgebra` provides fast linear algebra primitives that operate
seamlessly on base `matrix` objects and
\[[`bigmemory::big.matrix`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/bigmemory/man/big.matrix.html)\]
containers. The package wraps BLAS and LAPACK routines with R-friendly
helpers so that vector updates, matrix products, and classic
decompositions work the same way in memory or on disk.

## Package highlights

- **big.matrix workflows** – Guidance on creating, sharing, and cleaning
  up file-backed matrices is collected in the [Working with big.matrix
  Objects
  vignette](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/articles/big-matrix-workflows.html).
- **Vector kernels** – Level 1 BLAS-style helpers such as
  [`dset()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dset.md),
  [`dsub()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dsub.md)
  and
  [`ddot()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/ddot.md)
  extend familiar vector algebra to `big.matrix` inputs. See the [Level
  1 BLAS-Style Helpers
  vignette](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/articles/level-1-blas-style-helpers.html).
- **Matrix products** – Wrappers including
  [`dgemm()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgemm.md)
  and
  [`dsymm()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dsymm.md)
  expose Level 3 BLAS routines for dense matrix multiplication with
  optional file-backed outputs. Explore the [Matrix Wrapper Helpers
  vignette](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/articles/matrix-wrapper-helpers.html).
- **LAPACK decompositions** – QR, Cholesky, eigenvalue, and SVD helpers
  ([`dgeqrf()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgeqrf.md),
  [`dpotrf()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dpotrf.md),
  [`dgeev()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgeev.md),
  [`dgesdd()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgesdd.md))
  bring advanced factorisations to large datasets. Walk through the
  [LAPACK Decompositions
  vignette](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/articles/lapack-decompositions.html).

## Package options

The package defines a number of global options that begin with
`bigalgebra`:

Option Default value \* `bigalgebra.temp_pattern` with default `matrix_`
\* `bigalgebra.tempdir` with default `tempdir` \*
`bigalgebra.mixed_arithmetic_returns_R_matrix` with default `TRUE` \*
`bigalgebra.DEBUG` with default `FALSE`

The `bigalgebra.tempdir` option must be a function that returns a
temporary directory path used to store big matrix results of BLAS and
LAPACK operations. The default value is simply the base R
[`tempdir()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/tempfile.html) function.

The `bigalgebra.temp_pattern` option is a name prefix for file names of
generated big matrix objects output as a result of BLAS and LAPACK
operations.

The `bigalgebra.mixed_arithmetic_returns_R_matrix` option determines
whether arithmetic operations involving an R matrix or vector and a
`big.matrix` matrix or vector return a big matrix (when the option is
`FALSE`), or return a normal R matrix (`TRUE`).

## BLAS and LAPACK backends

The package is built, by default, with R’s native BLAS libraries, which
use 32-bit signed integer indexing. The default build is limited to
vectors of at most 2^31 − 1 entries and matrices with at most 2^31 − 1
rows and 2^31 − 1 columns (note that standard R matrices are limited to
2^31 − 1 total entries).

The package includes a reference BLAS implementation that supports
64-bit integer indexing, relaxing the limitation on vector lengths and
matrix row and column limits. Installation of this package with the
64-bit reference BLAS implementation may be performed from the
command-line install:

`REFBLAS=1 R CMD INSTALL bigalgebra`

where `bigalgebra` is the source package (for example,
`bigalgebra_0.9.0.tar.gz`).

The package may also be built with user-supplied external BLAS and
LAPACK libraries, in either 32- or 64-bit varieties. This is an advanced
topic that requires additional `Makevars` modification, and may include
adjustment of the low-level calling syntax depending on the library
used.

Feel free to contact us for help installing and running the package.

This website, the unit tests, some C code fixes and improvements as well
as these examples were created by F. Bertrand.

Maintainer: Frédéric Bertrand <frederic.bertrand@lecnam.net>.

## Installation

You can install the released version of bigalgebra from
[CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org) with:

``` r
install.packages("bigalgebra")
```

You can install the development version of bigalgebra from
[GitHub](https://github.com) with:

``` r
devtools::install_github("fbertran/bigalgebra")
```

## Quick tour of the functionality

The snippets below mirror the worked examples in the vignettes and show
how the helpers behave with in-memory and file-backed matrices.

### Level 1 BLAS helpers

These helpers cover vector updates, reductions, and element-wise
transforms such as the in-place square root provided by
[`dsqrt()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dsqrt.md).

``` r
library(bigmemory)
library(bigalgebra)

x <- bigmemory::big.matrix(5, 1, init = 0)
dset(ALPHA = 9, X = x)
dsqrt(X = x)
x[]
#> [1] 3 3 3 3 3

y <- bigmemory::big.matrix(5, 1, init = 1)
dvcal(ALPHA = 0.5, X = x, BETA = 2, Y = y)
y[]
#> [1] 3.5 3.5 3.5 3.5 3.5
```

### Matrix products with `dgemm()`

``` r
A <- bigmemory::big.matrix(5, 4, init = 1)
B <- bigmemory::big.matrix(4, 4, init = 2)
C <- bigmemory::big.matrix(5, 4, init = 0)

dgemm(A = A, B = B, C = C, ALPHA = 1, BETA = 0)
C[]
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]    8    8    8    8
#> [2,]    8    8    8    8
#> [3,]    8    8    8    8
#> [4,]    8    8    8    8
#> [5,]    8    8    8    8
```

### LAPACK decompositions

``` r
set.seed(1)
M <- matrix(rnorm(9), 3)
SPD <- crossprod(M)
SPD_big <- as.big.matrix(SPD)
dpotrf(A = SPD_big)
#> [1] 0
chol_factor <- SPD_big[,]
chol_factor[lower.tri(chol_factor)] <- 0
chol_factor
#>          [,1]       [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,] 1.060398 -0.2388263 -0.6138286
#> [2,] 0.000000  1.8082109  0.2222424
#> [3,] 0.000000  0.0000000  0.8294922
```

### File-backed `big.matrix` workflows

``` r
tmpdir <- tempdir()
file_big <- filebacked.big.matrix(3, 3, init = diag(3),
                                  backingpath = tmpdir,
                                  backingfile = "example.bin")
#> Warning in filebacked.big.matrix(3, 3, init = diag(3), backingpath = tmpdir, : No descriptor file given, it will be
#> named example.bin.desc
file_big[1, 3] <- 5
file_big[]
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    1    1    5
#> [2,]    1    1    1
#> [3,]    1    1    1
rm(file_big)
gc()
#>           used (Mb) gc trigger  (Mb) limit (Mb) max used (Mb)
#> Ncells  986811 52.8    1924765 102.8         NA  1419161 75.8
#> Vcells 2376145 18.2    8388608  64.0      65536  3616431 27.6
```

## Available vignettes

The full vignette set expands on the topics above and demonstrates how
the routines interact:

1.  **Working with big.matrix Objects** – Managing shared memory, file
    backing, and clean-up for large datasets.
2.  **Level 1 BLAS-Style Helpers** – Filling vectors, Hadamard products,
    and reductions on disk-backed data.
3.  **Matrix Wrapper Helpers** – Symmetric and general matrix products,
    including strategies for chaining operations.
4.  **LAPACK Decompositions with bigalgebra** – QR, Cholesky,
    eigenvalue, and SVD workflows for both in-memory and file-backed
    matrices.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`%*%,big.matrix,big.matrix-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  [`%*%,matrix,big.matrix-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  [`%*%,big.matrix,matrix-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  [`Arith,big.matrix,big.matrix-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  [`Arith,big.matrix,matrix-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  [`Arith,matrix,big.matrix-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  [`Arith,big.matrix,numeric-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  [`Arith,numeric,big.matrix-method`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/Ops.md)
  :

  Class `"big.matrix"` arithmetic methods

- [`bigalgebra-package`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/bigalgebra-package.md)
  [`bigalgebra`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/bigalgebra-package.md)
  : Arithmetic routines for native R matrices and big.matrix objects.

- [`dadd()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dadd.md) :
  Add two double-precision vectors.

- [`dasum()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dasum.md)
  : Sum of absolute values

- [`daxpy()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/daxpy.md)
  : BLAS daxpy functionality

- [`dcopy()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dcopy.md)
  : Copy a vector.

- [`ddot()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/ddot.md) :
  Dot product of two vectors

- [`dgeev()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgeev.md)
  : DGEEV computes eigenvalues and eigenvectors.

- [`dgemm()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgemm.md)
  : Matrix Multiply

- [`dgeqrf()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgeqrf.md)
  : QR factorization

- [`dgesdd()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dgesdd.md)
  : DGESDD computes the singular value decomposition (SVD) of a real
  matrix.

- [`dhprod()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dhprod.md)
  : Element-wise (Hadamard) product

- [`dnrm2()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dnrm2.md)
  : Euclidean norm (2-norm)

- [`dpotrf()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dpotrf.md)
  : Cholesky factorization

- [`dprdct()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dprdct.md)
  : Product of vector elements

- [`dqddot()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dqddot.md)
  : High-accuracy dot product

- [`dscal()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dscal.md)
  : Scales a vector by a constant.

- [`dset()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dset.md) :
  Fill a vector or matrix with a constant value

- [`dsqrt()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dsqrt.md)
  : Element-wise square root

- [`dsub()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dsub.md) :
  In-place vector subtraction

- [`dsum()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dsum.md) :
  Sum of elements

- [`dswap()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dswap.md)
  : Swap two double-precision vectors.

- [`dsymm()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dsymm.md)
  : Symmetric matrix-matrix multiplication

- [`dvcal()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dvcal.md)
  : Generalised AXPBY operation

- [`dxyz()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/dxyz.md) :
  Three-dimensional cross product

- [`idamax()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/idamax.md)
  : Index of the maximum absolute value

- [`idamin()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/idamin.md)
  : Index of the minimum absolute value

- [`idmax()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/idmax.md)
  : Index of the maximum element

- [`idmin()`](https://fbertran.github.io/bigalgebra/reference/idmin.md)
  : Index of the minimum element
